set_message.text: Skipping...Error messages are possible. They are an effect of the skip. Mission continues as normal. Confirm error(s)

then.#comment: User request 2026-10-26 (flight log: the pilot answer to the greeting waited 10 s behind the technician logbook and fuel lines and the copilot answer was dropped by the voice queue): the greetings of the three come first, the logbook and fuel talk starts when the exchange of greetings is over (vhg_greeting, set by voice hangar greeting).

crew reboard snapshot.#comment: Second dispatch accepted while the crew is outside (deboarding in progress or finished walking): the positions of the crew actors that exist now survive reload_mission in L:REBOARD_* (LAT/LON), and crew reboard interrupted crew recreates them there at the start of crew boarding so they walk back to their doors from where they are. An actor that does not exist is not stored: its seat was never left, or the normal boarding handles it.

crew reboard interrupted crew.#comment: Boarding of the crew that was outside when the second dispatch was accepted (see crew reboard snapshot). Same door, seat trigger and payload station as deboarding, in the reverse direction, starting from the stored position.

then.#comment: Sarah voice https://www.naturalreaders.com/online/ voice EN Bella

voice app connect.#comment: Voice app mode (L:AUDIOINHIBIT 1, voice code APP): connects to the voice server of the HPG Mission Companion at once, declares the voice pack EN (version 2 at least), makes the checklist voice (actor 11) the voice of every text without an actor tag and asks for new crew names. The pack texts are chosen by the program when the mission increments the LVARs L:xxxAPPnn; free texts (dispatch) are spoken with speak.

voice app lost.#comment: The Mission Companion is not there (the voice server refused or dropped the connection, or never answered, see voice app check). Only for the app selection (L:AUDIOINHIBIT not 0 and not 100): the mission goes back to the last selection of the user, the wav voice pack (VCP = VOICEPACK, L:AUDIOINHIBIT 0 as the original thread does when the external program is off), so that the sound LVARs play the wavs, and tells the user once per simulator session (L:HMC_APP_POPUP_SHOWN). With a wav pack selected nothing is shown. The Companion that starts later writes L:AUDIOINHIBIT 1 again and the thread EXTERNAL XML AUDIO ENABLE connects it. Tester report 2026-10-18: Companion not connected, TTS 0 and AUDIOINHIBIT 1 left silence for every voice and sound.

state.text: VCP now {0} (set in voice app lost): AUDIOINHIBIT={1} TTS={2}
VCP now {0} (set in voice app lost): AUDIOINHIBIT={1} TTS={2}

voice app popup.#comment: One popup for the whole simulator session (L:HMC_APP_POPUP_SHOWN, an LVAR: it survives a mission reload and is cleared when the flight is loaded again): the Companion is not connected. Called only by voice app lost, which runs for the app selection and never with a wav pack.

set_modal.title: Mission Companion not connected
set_modal.text: The voice and sound app is selected but it is not running or not connected. The mission uses the wav voice pack you selected until the Companion is started: it then connects by itself. This message is shown once.

voice app check.#comment: Called when a message is requested (voice say) or by the thread every second while the voice code is APP and the voice server is not connected (TTS not 1): after 25 s from the connection attempt without an answer the connection counts as lost (voice app lost), in case the on_disconnected callback never comes.

voice dispatcher publish.#comment: Tells the Mission Companion who the dispatcher is (user request of 2026-10-16): the tag <dsp:INDEX:CITY>, INDEX the position of the group selected on the CARLS in the static GRPID (global GRPIDX, -1 for the manual frequency), CITY the city of the base found by voice dispatcher name start (empty until found). The program keeps the last one until another arrives and says the full name of the group in its own words ({@DSP} in the pack, for example Leitstelle Zuerich); the mission keeps only the short names of GRPID. Called at the connection, when the group is chosen on the CARLS and when the city is known. Mission Companion only.

voice dispatcher name start.#comment: At the connection with the Mission Companion: publishes the dispatcher at once (city empty) and looks for the city of the base, the closest place (city, town or village) to mission_start_location within 20 km with the same kind of query as the closest hospital; the name of the result is base_city_Name. The wait for the base and for the query is at most 60 s and 45 s. The city is cleared at every call, so a city of an earlier mission never stays. When the query fails the program says the name without the city (Leitstelle, regional control center). Not run before a test in the simulator: the place query is not proven there yet (docs/testing/RUNTIME_VALIDATION.md).

voice new shift.#comment: New shift: the program draws new crew names when its option is Random names, and a new voice for the dispatcher when that actor is set to Random voice (the tags are ignored otherwise).

voice radio ready.#comment: 1 when the radio of the helicopter works for the Mission Companion rules of 2026-10-18: powered (the battery master or the GPCP power switch on) and the CARLS connected (L:CARLS_CONNECTED 1). The same rule the program applies to every radio line; a dispatch that arrives with it false is only a notification on the tablet.

voice radio reminder.#comment: User request of 2026-10-20: after a dispatch is accepted, if the helicopter is on (the battery master or the GPCP power switch) and the CARLS is still not connected after a few minutes, a crew member aboard, chosen at random, reminds the pilot to switch the radio on to talk to the dispatcher (pack RAD.REM). First reminder 3 to 5 minutes after the briefing started, then every 4 to 6 minutes, at most three. It stops when the radio works (voice radio ready), with a newer dispatch (voice_dispatch_seq) or when the mission is over (MISSION_PHASE 10 or more). With the helicopter off it only waits. Mission Companion only (a wav pack has no such line). param seq = the number of the dispatch.

voice crew member ok.#comment: 1 when the crew member (param member 2 doctor, 3 copilot, 4 HEMS 1, 5 HEMS 2) can speak: it exists (CREW_MEMBER_CAP), is not dead, not below 15 (the mute threshold of the context for the Mission Companion), and with aboard 1 is aboard (CREW_OUT_n 0); param skip is a member that does not count (the casualty).

voice crew speaker.#comment: The actor number (2 copilot, 3 doctor, 4 HEMS 1, 5 HEMS 2) of the crew member who speaks, 0 when nobody can (the pilot is the user and never counts). Param first: copilot (the designated one for the radio: if the copilot is missing, dead or unfit the next survivor speaks) or doc; param aboard 1 = only a member aboard; param skip = a member who does not count. The order after the first one: doctor, HEMS 1, HEMS 2, copilot.

voice read dispatch.#comment: The dispatcher (actor 8, external radio) reads the dispatch description and objective shown on the tablet. The description is a text with a key, DSC.<incident ID_CARD>.<variant 1-4>, so a translated pack of the Mission Companion speaks its own text; the shown English follows the key and is spoken when the pack has no such text or it does not match. The vehicle of the missions 65-67 is read apart (DSC.VEH). Then the crew briefing. Only with the Mission Companion (voice code APP). Mission description runs for every dispatch received (first, next, custom menu); vrd_last stops a second reading of the same text.

then.#comment: User rules of 2026-10-18 (cold dispatch): with the radio working (voice radio ready: power and the CARLS) the dispatcher reads the dispatch and the objective; without it the dispatch is only a notification on the tablet (the program says nothing of the dispatcher) and a crew member aboard, or partly aboard, reads the message back to the crew by voice: hey crew, a dispatch came in, what do we do? The call to the dispatcher for more information and the confirmation come when the radio is on (voice briefing chat), the dispatcher asks again for the confirmation (DSA.NUDGE) and says the reassignment as before.

voice crew all aboard.#comment: 1 when every crew member of this flight is aboard (L:HMC_CREW_PRESENT equals L:HMC_CREW_EXIST, both published by voice context for the Mission Companion), else 0. User rule 2026-10-24: the crew discusses a dispatch only when all of them are inside; the hangar greetings come first.

voice dsp gate.#comment: The crew talk about a dispatch stops while the dispatcher speaks on the radio (vda_dsp 1, set around the DSA.NUDGE and the DSA.REASSIGN lines) and goes on after the dispatcher part (user rule 2026-10-24).

voice dispatch nudge.#comment: The dispatcher asks for the confirmation once, a minute after the dispatch and as soon as the radio works (a dispatch read while the helicopter was cold stays only on the tablet until the radio is on). It runs in its own thread, so it can come while the crew is still discussing: the discussion waits (voice dsp gate) and goes on after the dispatcher. Param seq = the number of the dispatch.

voice dispatch readback.#comment: The readback of a dispatch heard with the radio off (user rules of 2026-10-18): a crew member aboard, or partly aboard, reads the message back to the crew by voice and asks what to do. Called by voice read dispatch when the dispatch arrives with somebody aboard, and by voice dispatch triage run when the crew boards later (flight log of 2026-10-19: the dispatch arrived with nobody aboard, the crew boarded and nobody said anything). Uses vrd_text and vrd_veh of voice read dispatch; sets vrd_rb 1 once it has been said.

then.#comment: User report 2026-10-20: the readback was in a plain voice with the helicopter powered. The text carries no radio tag now: the Mission Companion decides (the intercom with the battery or the GPCP switch on, the voice without power; the pack messages DSA.RB.A and DSA.RB.Q say radio ics).

voice dispatch triage.#comment: A dispatch arrived by RescueTrack (ready dispatch, first_dispatch: vda_pending yes) and the dispatcher read it: the crew decides before the pilot (the user) accepts on the tablet. The copilot asks the crew (DSA.ASK); with a second dispatch the fuel against the LOWFUELTHRSLD option (DSA.FUEL.OK / LOW), the two missions of the shift (DSA.MIS, the old PLT38 rule), the equipment (DSA.EQP) and the health (DSA.HLT) are checked; then DSA.GO and the question to the pilot (DSA.ASKP, or DSA.ASKP.B with fuel low or two missions done). The briefing with the dispatcher (voice briefing chat) waits for the acceptance: voice dispatch accepted, called by accept_dispatch. voice_dispatch_seq numbers the dispatches: a thread that is not the last one stops. Only with the Mission Companion (a wav pack keeps the counters PLT38 and PLT40).

voice dispatch triage run.#comment: Thread of voice dispatch triage (params seq = the number of this dispatch, second = 1 for a second dispatch). Lines 1.5 s apart; the chatter (declut 1) follows the AUDIO_DECLUT levels, the fuel warning, the two missions and the question to the pilot are always said. Then it waits for the acceptance (vda_open no, set by voice dispatch accepted) or a newer dispatch (voice_dispatch_seq changed) and, the dispatcher nudge is a thread of its own (voice dispatch nudge) and the crew lines wait for it (voice dsp gate).

Flight log of 2026-10-19: the dispatch arrived with nobody aboard (the program drops the lines of the crew then), the crew boarded a minute later and nobody said a word. The triage now waits until a crew member is aboard (it gives up after 30 minutes, with a newer dispatch or when the dispatch is accepted), then reads a dispatch heard with the radio off back to the crew (voice dispatch readback), then the questions follow.

User rule 2026-10-24 (flight log: the dispatch arrived while the technician was still chatting with only the copilot aboard, and the readback was dropped by the voice queue): the hangar greetings stay, they come before the boarding and nobody reads the tablet yet. The discussion of the crew starts when all of them are aboard and the greetings are over; if somebody is still missing two minutes after the first one boarded it starts anyway.

do.#comment: With the radio off (a dispatch that stays only on the tablet) the crew asks the pilot again once, a minute after the question (user, flight log of 2026-10-19: the crew sat aboard for four minutes with the dispatch waiting and said nothing).

voice dispatch reassign.#comment: Called by ready dispatch when the new dispatch arrives: if the previous one was never accepted (vda_open yes) the dispatcher says it was reassigned to another unit (DSA.REASSIGN) and the waiting thread of the old one stops. The new dispatch is read afterwards by Mission description.

voice dispatch accepted.#comment: Called by accept_dispatch when the pilot accepts on the tablet: the answer to the dispatcher and the briefing (voice briefing chat) go on. A second dispatch reloads the mission, which ends every thread: L:VDA_RESP asks for the briefing to be said after the reload (loading macro, Cabin preparation completed). Without the triage (a wav pack, a custom mission) vda_open is not yes and nothing happens.

voice day period.#comment: The part of the day of the simulator (its local time): 1 morning (05:00 to 11:59), 2 afternoon (12:00 to 17:59), 3 evening (18:00 to 04:59). Used to say good morning, good afternoon or good evening.

voice weather class.#comment: User request of 2026-10-19: the weather where the helicopter is, for the remarks of the crew and the weather of the briefing. Sets vw_dir (wind direction in tens of degrees), vw_spd (wind knots), vw_tmp (temperature in Celsius), vw_vis (visibility in km, 10 means 10 or more), vw_sfx (the suffix of the pack keys) and returns the class: 1 light rain (RL), 2 heavy rain (RH, rate 3 or more), 3 snow (SN), 4 hot from 30 C (HT), 5 cold up to 4 C (CD), 6 freezing up to -5 C (FZ), 7 fog under 3 km (FG), 8 wind from 20 knots (WD), 9 fine weather (FR: 12 to 26 C, wind under 12 knots, visibility 9 km or more), 0 nothing to say. The first class that applies wins, in this order. AMBIENT PRECIP STATE: 2 none, 4 rain, 8 snow. The thresholds of the precipitation rate and of the classes are to tune in the simulator.

voice weather brief.#comment: The copilot reads the weather in the mission briefing (WXB.<class>, with the wind direction and speed, the temperature and the visibility; WXB.OK when nothing is remarkable). Called at the end of the briefing thread, which already follows the chatter levels. Only with the Mission Companion.

voice deboarding chat.#comment: At the hangar after the flight, when the technician is there (param stage): 1 = a remark about the weather (WXD.<class>) and the answer of the copilot (WXC.<class>), before the thanks of the pilot (PLT 8); 2 = after it, the farewell of the technician by the hour of the simulator (DEB.BYE.TEC.M, A, E) and the answer of the pilot (DEB.BYE.PLT). Called by deboarding inside the chatter levels of its original lines. Only with the Mission Companion.

voice hangar greeting.#comment: User request of 2026-10-19 (flight log: the technician said one 'Hi all', the copilot 'Good morning!' at night, and that was all): at the hangar the technician, the copilot and the pilot greet each other by the hour of the simulator and by name (GRT.TEC / GRT.CPL / GRT.PLT with the suffix M morning, A afternoon, E evening), then a few words of the circumstances (CHT.TEC, CHT.CPL) and the farewell of the technician (CHT.TEC2). Only with the Mission Companion (voice code APP and the voice server connected), and with the chatter levels of the original lines (AUDIO_DECLUT 0 or above 3). The wav packs keep FRA 7 and CPL 23. Called by the boarding of the copilot while the technician is present.

voice boarding chat.#comment: Crew conversation after the comm check (pack EN group board): pilot asks, copilot, doctor and the rear crew answer, pilot closes. New LVAR numbers PLT 47-48, CPL 65, PAX3 38, 90 (no wav yet). Only with the Mission Companion.

crew voice profile apply.#comment: Which of the 5 crews of synthetic voices the Mission Companion uses (user request of 2026-10-25, Companion 1.2.51: L:CREW_PROFILE 1 to 5, 0 or not set keeps the last choice of the program). The global CREW_PROFILE (option of the audio tab, saved in the profiles, 1 at the first start) is written to the LVAR; a livery that sets L:LIVERY_CREWPROFILE to 1 to 5 overrides it when L:LIVERY_ACTIVATION is 1 and the settings are not forced over the livery, with the same conditions as L:LIVERY_CREW. The program may override the LVAR for a while: that is not a choice, the global is not touched.

failure crew announce.#comment: In flight the pilot and the copilot announce a random failure (user request of 2026-10-25): either one says what failed and the other verifies (Check / Verified), or one says that there is a failure and the other says which. Called by the failure engine (not by the crash tiers) with param code. The failure type is kept for the report to the technician (failure tech report). Mission Companion only; without it the old copilot line CPL 9 is played.

failure crew speak.#comment: Speaks the failure of the locals fa_type and fa_arg (set by failure crew announce or by the fuel leakage thread). The speaker (1 pilot, 2 copilot) and the manner are drawn; the other member verifies or says which. Keys FLT.<type> of the pack (argument {0} = engine or system number), FLT.GEN, FLT.CHK, FLT.CHIPV (verification of the MGB chip with the proposal of the chip burn).

failure tech report.#comment: At the deboarding the technician answers the failures that the crew verified in flight (FR_<type>, set by failure crew speak) with the repair time of each component, then the flags are cleared. Keys FTR.<type> of the pack; {0} = engine or system number.

failure tech clear.#comment: RESET FAILURES repairs the helicopter: the verified failures waiting for the report to the technician are cleared too.

voice impact ask.#comment: After an impact that hurt somebody (voice crew impact): the pilot asks the crew for their status and, with a patient on the stretcher (L:SDK_CABIN_PAX_5 = 2), the copilot asks the doctor about the patient and the doctor answers. Pack IMP.*.

voice hoist all inside.#comment: The hoisted persons are all inside, the hook and the boom are stowed: the rear crew tells the pilot, who cannot see behind, that everybody is inside and that he is clear to leave the hover (pack PAX1.INS, user request of 2026-10-25 after the report of MPR on PAX1.14). Without the Mission Companion the old line PAX1.18 (hook in, boom retracted) is played. PAX1.14 only says that the hoist is up and that the last persons are being brought in.

voice crew out clear.#comment: A crew member stays on the ground (the medic travels with the ambulance or goes to the patient, the heli rescuers are dropped): once the doors are closed, the hook is in and the boom retracted, the rear crew tells the pilot that he is clear to leave the hover (pack PAX1.OUT; user request of 2026-10-25). Without the Mission Companion the old line PAX1.18 is played.

voice briefing chat.#comment: Crew briefing after the dispatcher read the dispatch (pack EN group brief). New LVAR numbers PLT 49-50, CPL 66, PAX3 39, 91. Starts with voice dispatch exchange (the pilot asks the dispatcher for an update, the dispatcher answers by mission class). Also starts the reminder to switch the radio on (voice radio reminder, user request of 2026-10-20).

else.#comment: Radio not on yet: the crew calls the dispatcher as soon as it is (within 15 minutes, not for an older dispatch), asking for more information and confirming the tasking.

voice debrief chat.#comment: Crew debriefing on the ground at the base: LIFESCORE above 3 the good outcome (pack EN group debriefok, PLT 51-52, CPL 67, PAX3 40, 92), otherwise the bad one (debriefbad, PLT 53-54, CPL 68, PAX3 41). Only with the Mission Companion.

voice approach briefing.#comment: Two nautical miles from the accident, after the rescue vehicles information of the tablet (RESCUE_DISPATCHED): the dispatcher says in ONE sentence which vehicles are on scene and which are on the way (AVAIL 1 = on scene from the start, 2 = dispatched; the arrived flags move a vehicle to the scene), then the crew briefing: pilot (ground or hoist plan: hoist when there is no landing_spot or it is farther from the patient than ldg_spot_area_size), copilot (police or fire there or not), doctor (ambulance or not), crew chief (ground or hoist), pilot. Only information the crew has at that moment: the dispatch and the vehicles it announced. Pack EN keys DSP.VEH.* and APR.*; only with the Mission Companion (VCP APP). For a patient transfer and an organ transport (voice mission class TRF and ORG) the same moment, two nautical miles from the pickup point, has its own short briefing instead (pack EN APR.TRF.* and APR.ORG.*): no vehicles, no accident. Plan P (police): when the landing spot is chosen (customLZ), the police is on scene or on the way and the patient is farther than police_bring_crew_min_dist from the landing spot, the pilot says the distance and that the police drives the crew (APR.PLT.P with the distance in meters, rounded to 50, and APR.CHF.P), whatever the hoist or ground plan.

then.#comment: Information of the mission for the approach (uniform with the other briefings): more than one patient expected (HELOVICTIMS), fire at the scene (random_fire yes or forced).

voice midway briefing.#comment: Two nautical miles from the meeting point of a midway meeting (L:MIDWAY 1: the ambulance brings the patient half way, the user accepted the point): the crew briefing for this kind of mission, like the ones of the organ transport and the patient transfer (pack EN APR.MID.*). Mission Companion only; chatter, skipped by the AUDIO_DECLUT levels 1 to 3.

voice role code.#comment: The role code of the pack names for a crew member number (1 pilot, 2 doctor, 3 copilot, 4 HEMS 1, 5 HEMS 2): PLT, PAX3, CPL, PAX1, PAX2. The texts of the pack take it with {role:0} and say the job word of their language.

voice crew hurt.#comment: A crew member hurt by an impact complains with his own voice (user request of 2026-10-18: nobody said anything after the crash): CEM.HURT while the score is under 90, CEM.WEAK when he is critical (10 or less); nothing for a death. param member 1 pilot, 2 doctor, 3 copilot, 4 HEMS 1, 5 HEMS 2. The speaking actor is the one of the member (1 pilot, 3 doctor, 2 copilot, 4, 5).

voice crash cry.#comment: A crew member who dies in a crash may cry out at the impact (user rules 2026-10-25): only a crew member (never a patient), only at the impact, at random (about 6 times in 10), one short sound at low volume and without the radio effect, never the long scream of the fall of a hoist operator (L:DEAD). Seven sounds, SYS.CRY1 to SYS.CRY7 of the pack (the files AND.crash.*.wav of the Companion). Called by voice crew impact when an evaluated member has CREW_LIFESCORE_n 0 or less. Mission Companion only.

voice crew impact.#comment: After an impact (called first by crew impact events): the members hurt complain, then a crew member who is fine says what he sees: a death (CEM.DEAD) or a critical member (CEM.CRIT). The evaluation flags are copied into locals because crew impact events clears them. Mission Companion only. A member who died in the impact may cry out first (voice crash cry).

voice crew event.#comment: A crew member died or is critical (called by crew member event announce, params member and kind death or critical): the radio call to the dispatcher is made by the designated member, the copilot; when the copilot is missing, dead or unfit the surviving member makes it (user, 2026-10-18); then the dispatcher answers. Mission Companion only; with the radio off (power or CARLS) the program does not play the call and the tablet messages remain.

voice crew divert.#comment: The mission is aborted by a crew emergency (crew emergency divert): with the crew outside the doctor says that he comes back and the patient stays for the next unit (CEM.OPS), otherwise a crew member says that the mission is aborted (CEM.ABORT). Mission Companion only.

voice crew continue.#comment: The user chose Continue after a critical crew member (crew emergency continue): a crew member acknowledges it (CEM.CONT). Mission Companion only.

voice mayday.#comment: Critical failure (engine fire, engine failure, gearbox damage: critical failure mayday, param kind F fire, E engine, G gearbox): a crew member aboard tells to land (MAY.REACT), the designated member, the copilot or the surviving one, calls the mayday on the radio (MAY.CALL.F, E or G) and the dispatcher answers (MAY.DSP). Mission Companion only.

voice sar briefing.#comment: Briefing of the crew for a search and rescue mission (user request of 2026-10-18), Mission Companion only: the kind of search (SAR, SARV overdue vehicle, SARC parked car, SARH person away from home: voice mission class), what is known (the search area with its radius, or the route and the last contact when there is no ring; the vehicle with its colour and model when the dispatch gives them), how the area is divided (sectors of 45 degrees and legs spaced twice the spotting range for the ring, the legs along the road for the route), the clock positions of the crew, and the best altitude and speed (the logic of SAR sighting: the spotting range is the full SPOTTED_DISTANCE at 1000 ft above the ground and up to 80 knots, below or above and faster it shrinks). Called one nautical mile before the search ring, or just after the take-off when the mission has no ring.

voice heli rescuer briefing.#comment: Briefing of the crew to the heli rescuer(s) who just boarded (user request of 2026-10-17: it is the crew, not the rescuer who knows nothing, who explains the roles and the situation). Called from pick heli rescuer hoist and pick heli rescuer ground, inside the thread that used to count the old one-sentence briefing (PAX3 25). Returns 1 when the briefing was spoken, 0 when the caller must keep the old counter (wav packs, no voice server, AUDIO_DECLUT 1 to 3, a scene closer than 2 minutes). Mission Companion only (VCP APP). Pack EN HRB.*, group hrbrief: the pilot opens with the kind of mission and the injured (HRB.OPEN.<ACC|SAR|SARV|SARC|SARH|TRF|ORG>, INJ counts as ACC), the copilot gives the time to the scene and the ground units (HRB.ETA, HRB.VEH.*), the doctor says what is known medically (HRB.MED.*), the rear crew chief (the copilot when the flight has fewer than 4 crew members, CREW_MEMBER_CAP) explains the two sequences: ground (HRB.PLAN.G.*: the rescuer leaves first by the left door, secures the area and calls it, the crew follows on that call, the rescuer boards last) and hoist (HRB.PLAN.H.*: the rescuer is lowered first, the winch operator runs the cable, the crew is lowered on the rescuer's call, the rescuer is the last on the cable); both are briefed because the pilot chooses on scene (L:MISSION_HOIST), the mission does not know it yet. With CREW CHATTER on FULL the briefing is interactive: the pilot asks for questions, the rescuer asks one of three (who gives the go, a hazard or more patients, what is needed on the ground) or none and the answer follows, the doctor and the copilot may voice a doubt that the pilot or the rescuer answers, the rescuer reads back the sequence and the doctor and the chief confirm. With 5 minutes or more to the scene (accident_location, 120 kt) the briefing is complete, from 2 to 5 minutes it is short (open, the two sequences, the readback, the close). TRF and ORG have no scene: open, doctor, the rescuer stays aboard and helps, readback, close. The local hrb_busy keeps voice calm at 0 and the cruise chat waiting while the briefing is spoken.

voice vehicle letters.#comment: The rescue vehicles of the tablet as letters for the voice texts: vb_s = the vehicles on scene, vb_w = the ones still on the way (A ambulance, F fire engine, P police; AVAIL 1 = on scene from the start, 2 = dispatched, the arrived flags move a vehicle to the scene), vb_amb N or A (ambulance), vb_sec N or S (police or fire). Used by the approach briefing and by voice crew vehicles.

voice crew vehicles.#comment: The crew confirms the rescue vehicles of the tablet in ONE sentence (pack EN CRW.VEH.BOTH, SCENE, WAY; nothing when there are none), instead of one short line for each vehicle. Mission Companion only (VCP APP): the old counters stay for the wav packs.

voice hospital proposal.#comment: After Query closest hospital, on the way to the patient: waits for the hospital (45 s at most, same fallback as the crew emergency route). Found: PRE_HOSPITAL is saved as before and, with the Mission Companion (VCP APP), the doctor says its name (pack EN HOSP.FOUND, the name is the hospital_name of the query); the wav packs keep the old line (PAX3 counter 6). Not found: with the Mission Companion the doctor says that no hospital was found and that the destination will be chosen by hand (HOSP.NONE).

voice say.#comment: One line of the pack (Mission Companion, voice code APP): <say:KEY> with the argument a for {0}. declut 1 = chatter, skipped by the AUDIO_DECLUT levels 1 to 3 like the other conversations. Used by the macros below.

voice mission class.#comment: The kind of the mission for the voice texts: ACC accident, SAR search and rescue (SARV overdue vehicle, SARC parked car, SARH person away from a house), TRF patient transfer, ORG organ transport, INJ injured only. From the locals SAR, scene_macro and accident_name of the dispatch.

voice objective.#comment: The dispatcher says the objective of the mission in a colloquial way, a text for each kind of mission (pack EN OBJ.*), after reading the description of the dispatch.

voice ground update.#comment: Updates during the ground operations (called every 2 s by on-site operations progress monitor). The team reports when it has news, not on a timer: a new stage of the operations (deployment, treatment with the condition of the patient from LIFESCORE, CPR, loading, return; a dead patient has its own report), a change of the time left (TIMERGND times the progress that is missing, in minutes, at most one report every 20 s), once who transports the patient. When nothing happens for 240 s and the pilot is alone (nobody else aboard, L:HMC_CREW_PRESENT) the pilot asks for the status; when nothing happens for 150 s and somebody is aboard, they make small talk (voice banter, only when voice calm allows it). Only with the Mission Companion (VCP APP). Pack EN GRD.*.

then.#comment: The condition of the patient swings between stable and serious with the LIFESCORE (report 2026-10-23: the same time left was said four times): both count as one stage in the signature, so a report needs a new stage (critical, CPR, loading) or a new time left.

Tester report 2026-10-25 (GRD.ETA.0 right after the crew gets out): no time left is given while the estimate of the ground time does not exist yet (TIMERGND is 0 until the doctor's estimate is made) nor while the progress is still low and the computed time is under a minute; 'almost ready' is said only when the work is really nearly done.

voice patient died.#comment: A patient died (called by multipatient registry event DIED): the doctor says it and the pilot answers; after the impact of a hard landing the copilot asks first and the lines are about the impact (the death cause is not the clinical deterioration). Not more than one reading every 20 s. Pack EN DTH.*.

No scream for a patient (user correction 2026-10-25): the L:DEAD sound AND.dead.wav is the scream of a hoist operator who falls and is played only by the hoist casualties, never by a patient death. The survivors speak: with the Companion the pack DTH.*, with a wav pack the existing wav PAX3 7 (The patient has died.). Called by patient death notice after voice app lost, so VCP is never APP without the Companion at this point.

wav unit arrival.#comment: The crew tells that a ground unit arrived: the wavs of the spreadsheet docs/AND_voice_messages.xlsx that had no call site (user request 2026-10-18, triggers of its column E): PAX3 32 ambulance on scene (param unit ambulance), PAX3 34 police securing the scene (police), PAX3 35 fire service controlling a hazard (fire, only with a fire or smoke hazard: random_fire not no). The LVAR is the wav of the packs and, with the Companion, its pack message (same number). Only while the crew is on the way or on scene (MISSION_PHASE 5 to 7), once per unit in 120 s (an arrival is set by more than one parking branch).

then.#comment: An ambulance that arrives when the crew already loads or brings back the patient (whobringpatient us) takes nothing: no handover line (report 2026-10-23).

wav secondary rescue.#comment: The secondary rescue of ambulance 2 starts (ambulance2 secondary rescue, spreadsheet column E): PAX3 33 a second ambulance is managing another patient, keep the landing area clear; six seconds later, with more than one casualty (HELOVICTIMS 2 or more), PAX3 37 additional patients remain on scene, await tasking before departure. Crew on the way, on scene or flying (MISSION_PHASE 5 to 9); the secondary rescue starts once per dispatch.

patient death notice.#comment: Warning for a patient death in any phase (user request 2026-10-18), purely informational: called by multipatient registry event DIED, so it covers the live physiology step whatever the path (clinical deterioration, impact). The dispatch page and the briefing page are closed first (set_dispatch_dialog 0, set_briefing_dialog 0): a message does not appear over them. Then the red message, the sound and the voice (voice patient died). With the Companion selected but not connected the mission falls back to the wav pack before the sound (voice app lost). Tester report 2026-10-25: nothing is said or played for a death after the patient was handed over to the hospital (MISSION_PHASE 9 or later); the physiology of a handed-over patient also stops in the registry.

voice hard landing.#comment: After a hard landing (threads landing hard, copilot line CPL 39): the pilot asks the crew to report, the copilot and the doctor (when aboard) answer. Pack EN HLD.*.

voice hospital approach.#comment: Some minutes before the hospital (random distance 3.5 to 6.5 km from hospital_user, phase 8 or later) the copilot calls the hospital with the minutes to go (distance over ground speed; 90 kt when slower than 40) and the hospital answers that it waits at the helipad: a patient aboard, an organ (whobringpatient organ) or a patient who died. Once for each dispatch (it waits for a phase below 8 before it can speak again). Pack EN HOS.CALL.* and HOS.REPLY*.

voice sar found.#comment: User request of 2026-10-20: when the target of a search and rescue is found (SAR sighting, the landing spot is created) the copilot tells the dispatcher by radio, with the position of the target (degrees and minutes, approximate), and the dispatcher answers (SAR.FND.PLT, SAR.FND.A; arguments latitude degrees, minutes, N or S, longitude degrees, minutes, E or W). Mission Companion only; the radio rules of the program apply (powered and the CARLS connected, else nothing is heard).

voice hospital marshal expected.#comment: 1 when the marshal of the destination hospital will be there (the same condition as voice marshal notice and the creation of the hospital marshal: the option MARSHAL_HOSPITAL_ENABLED for a hospital that is not in the shared table, or the marshal of the table for a hospital that is) and he was not created yet; 0 otherwise.

voice hospital final.#comment: User report 2026-10-20 (few calls with the hospital): after the call with the minutes to go (voice hospital approach) the hospital is called again on the final approach, 900 m from the helipad (HOS.FIN.P the copilot asks to land, HOS.FIN.A the hospital clears with the wind: arguments wind direction and knots), when the helicopter is on the helipad (HOS.PAD.P, HOS.PAD.A) and when the crew is ready to leave (HOS.DEP.P, HOS.DEP.A, MISSION_PHASE 10 within 500 m). Once for each dispatch (it waits for a phase below 8 before it can speak again). Pack EN HOS.*; Mission Companion only (the lines are said only with VCP APP and TTS 1).

voice pickup approach.#comment: User request of 2026-10-20: a patient transfer or an organ transport tells the pick-up place that the helicopter is coming, some minutes before (random 3.5 to 6.5 km from userA, between phase 4 and 7): the copilot gives the minutes to go and asks to be ready (PCK.CALL.TRF or ORG, argument the minutes) and the place answers (PCK.REPLY.TRF or ORG, ground unit on the external radio). Once for each dispatch (it waits for a phase above 6 and then below 4). Mission Companion only.

voice organ briefing.#comment: User request of 2026-10-20: the briefing of an organ transport tells the organ (heart, liver, kidneys, lungs or pancreas: organ_type, drawn when the mission is made), the recipient (a name from the lists and an age: organ_rcp, organ_age) and the destination hospital (ORG.INF, the doctor), then whether the time is enough: vob_left the minutes left to the deadline (organexpiration), vob_need the minutes the flight needs (the distance to the pick-up and from the pick-up to the hospital with timemultiplier, the same formula that sets the deadline); OK when there are 10 minutes more than needed, TG (tight) with less, LT (late) when the need is more than the time left (ORG.TIM.OK, TG, LT, the copilot) and the reaction of the chief (ORG.RCT.OK, TG, LT). Then the thread voice organ watch follows the time. Mission Companion only.

voice organ watch.#comment: Follows the time of an organ transport (every 20 s, until the dispatch ends): when the minutes the flight still needs (before the pick-up: to userA and from there to the hospital; after it: to the hospital; with timemultiplier) become more than the minutes left to the deadline, the copilot says it once (ORG.WARN, arguments the minutes left and the minutes needed); when the deadline has passed (organcountdown below 0), once (ORG.LATE). param seq = the number of the dispatch (a newer one stops this thread). Mission Companion only.

voice organ handoff.#comment: User request of 2026-10-20: at the pick-up of the organ the ground team tells the crew what it is, for whom, how important it is and how much time is left, and the rear crew answers (ORG.PCK.G, the ground unit; ORG.PCK.R). Arguments organ, recipient, age, minutes left. Called by organ pick up scene1 after ORG.PCK. Mission Companion only.

voice marshal notice.#comment: The presence of the hospital marshal (same condition as the optional marshaller at the destination hospital) is told by the dispatcher at a random distance of 0.9 to 3 km from the hospital, before the arrival. Once for each dispatch. Pack EN MAR.NTC.H.

voice hospital handover.#comment: At the handover of the patient at the hospital, started when the crew meets the ground crew (the stretcher team next to the helicopter, before the unloading is finished and before the tablet message Patient handed over to ED): the hospital team welcomes the crew, the doctor gives the handover and the hospital thanks. Pack EN HOS.WEL, HOS.HND, HOS.THX (HOS.ORG for an organ).

voice calm.#comment: 1 when the mood allows small talk: no crew emergency, nobody hurt (every crew member of the flight has CREW_LIFESCORE 85 or more and is alive), and with the param patient 1 a patient that is not dying, not dead and not in CPR (LIFESCORE 50 or more), with the param casualties 1 nobody died in this session (PATIENTS_KILLED_TOTAL). Used by voice cruise chat, voice banter and voice tip. Always 0 when the setting CREW CHATTER is REDUCED or MINIMAL, except with the param tip 1 (voice tip: the tips have their own setting CREW TIPS, independent from the chatter). Also 0 while the crew briefs the heli rescuer (hrb_busy yes, voice heli rescuer briefing).

voice banter.#comment: Small talk of the crew (pack EN BAN.Y yesterday, BAN.M a match, BAN.C company): one of the three at random, four lines after a random 5 to 15 s. Only when voice calm says so (param patient and casualties as there); the messages are futile ones: options 1 and 2 are silent and the conversation stays coherent, so many times nothing is said.

voice tip.#comment: A tip of the crew about a function of the mission that pilots may not know (user request of 2026-10-14): a conversation of four lines, pack EN TIP.<topic>.1 to 4 (futile, spoken by the copilot, the doctor and sometimes the pilot), one after a random 5 to 15 s. Only when the setting CREW TIPS is on (the global CREW_TIPS, 0 or empty = on, 1 = off; kept in the profiles, independent from CREW CHATTER) and voice calm says so (param patient and casualties as in voice banter, param tip 1 so that the chatter setting does not stop it); with CREW CHATTER REDUCED or MINIMAL the Companion chooses the lower options of the message (all of them tell the whole information). The topics follow each other in a fixed order (SAV saves, MSL mission list presets, PRF settings profiles, CRW crew health, KIT kit weights, QLK quick links, DBG debug snapshots, MED medical options, FLR failures, CHT crew chatter, CND the option On conditions missions, TOF how to switch the tips off) from a random start, so a tip is not repeated before all the others were told (the local vtp_next survives the reloads). The key is built from the topic code and the line number; a wav pack (no TTS) says nothing.

voice cruise chat.#comment: Small talk during the long legs of the flight, once each: to the scene (phases 4 to 6, more than 7 km from accident_location, above 300 ft), to the hospital (phase 8 or 9, more than 7 km from hospital_user) and back to the base (route 6, more than 7 km from RTB_location). Only when voice calm allows it (never with a dying patient, an injured crew member, or after a death); a short chat of the pack (CRZ.*, futile) and then, by a roll of 0 to 9, a conversation of voice banter (0 to 3), a tip of voice tip (4 to 6) or nothing; on the way back to the base a banter (roll 0 to 4) or a tip. When voice calm refuses the chat (CREW CHATTER REDUCED or MINIMAL, or the mood) the leg still offers a tip, 4 times in 10 (5 in 10 back to the base), because the tips have their own setting CREW TIPS and voice tip decides by itself. Chatter (AUDIO_DECLUT).

voice context publish.#comment: Context for the radio rule of the Mission Companion, published only in voice app mode (L:AUDIOINHIBIT not 0) and only when it changes: L:HMC_HELI_OFF 1 = battery master off and rotor stopped; L:HMC_CREW_PRESENT = bit 0 pilot, 1 copilot, 2 doctor, 3 HEMS1, 4 HEMS2 aboard (the seat tracker CREW_OUT_n flags); L:HMC_CTX_VALID 1 = both are published. The program decides how a line is heard (intercom, radio, external radio, voice, far voice, nothing: rules in the Companion, docs/architecture/VOICE_APP_MODE.md). L:HMC_CREW_EXIST = same bits as CREW_PRESENT for the crew members that exist (CREW_MEMBER_CAP), aboard or not; L:HMC_AT_BASE = 1 while the helicopter is in the wifi range of the start base (local wifiinrange = in), where the dispatcher reaches the crew radios even with the battery off; L:HMC_ZONE_TECH and L:HMC_ZONE_GROUND = zone of the nearest technician (engineera, engineer) and of the nearest ground unit or hospital staff (marshall, ambumedic, ambumedic3) from the helicopter: 1 up to 5 m, 2 up to 30 m, 3 up to 100 m, 4 beyond, 0 no such object (macros voice zone nearest, voice zone class). The battery master is not published: the Companion reads the aircraft variable L:H145_SDK_OH_BATTERY_MASTER. All of them are part of the change signature. L:HMC_CREW_MUTE (same bits) = crew members who must not speak: dead (CREW_DEAD_n 1) or hurt so badly (CREW_LIFESCORE_n below 15) that they are out of the conversation; the Companion keeps their lines silent. L:HMC_CHAT_MAX = the highest option number the Companion may choose for a message (the setting CREW CHATTER: FULL 6, REDUCED 3 = professional wording and the futile lines at their default, MINIMAL 1 = the default wording only, the futile lines silent); it is part of the change signature.

then.#comment: Pilot = the simmer: aboard from the end of the boarding (the right cockpit door closes after the pilot object is destroyed) to the deboarding (removed after the right cockpit door opens). PILOT_OUT is 1 in between; the visible pilot model (IMPL_PILOT0) is not used because an option can hide it.

Crew members outside the helicopter (hoist_crew, pax1, pax2, pax3): nearest one, same classes as the technician. The program uses it to let the crew talk by voice by distance when there is no radio link (user decision 2026-10-25).

Choosing a linked MSN LIST loads this settings preset. Press the selected MSN LIST button again to remove the link.

Ground time.#comment: HEMS registry visits sleep TIMEnSHORT once per clinical step, so TIMEnSHORT is level dependent. TIMEnMED/TIMEnLONG are still consumed by patient_wait_interval (ambulance and legacy hoist flows) and are not part of the HEMS visit estimate.

Rough estimate only: the clinical visit (TIMERGND, unchanged because it also paces the progress bar) plus a fixed allowance for the crew walking out, loading and walking back (90 s each way, 90 s per casualty), rounded to whole minutes.

deboarding damage state.#comment: 1 when the helicopter comes back damaged or with a failure (user rule 2026-10-24): a crash, an overspeed or a flight limit event (L:CRASH, L:VNE, L:FLI), a damage of the engines or of the gearboxes of 85 percent or more, an engine failed or on fire, or any of the failures of the failure ladder. The same conditions as the pilot lines of the deboarding. Result in the param named by result.

service truck.#comment: The helicopter is back damaged and the crew is taken by the van (hangar farther than L:VANACTION): the copilot asks the dispatcher for technical assistance, the dispatcher confirms, and the technician arrives from the hangar with the Airbus H145 Service Truck (VAR 1 1 = lights on, left on while it waits), which stops 22 m behind the helicopter on the side closer to the hangar (rear sector: the van uses the front sector bearing 290 to 20 and the crew walk there). The truck is removed at the end of deboarding. Repair times: later.

set_message.text: Technical assistance requested: the service truck is coming from the hangar.
COMPLETE SHUT DOWN PROCEDURE AND SET THE BATTERY SWITCH TO OFF TO COMPLETE THE MISSION

deboarding.#comment: MISSION_END_WAITING is raised only at the end of the macro, when the copilot and the pilot have finished (deboard_pilot_done): the end menu never appears while somebody is still leaving the helicopter.

set_message.text: Open the pilot door to complete deboarding.
Crew is waiting you, they will wait another minute, then the van will go back.
Van is leaving without you. It will not return to pick you.

voice dispatch exchange.#comment: Dynamic briefing after the dispatcher read the dispatch (called by voice briefing chat with the mission class): the pilot asks the dispatcher for an update by radio and the dispatcher answers with what is useful for this kind of mission (pack EN DSP.RQ and DSP.ANS.ACC, INJ, SAR, TRF, ORG), then, now and then and only with CREW CHATTER on FULL, the crew presents itself on board (BRF.INT.*, futile lines).
